question.problem:
The joint CDF of two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

$$
F(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<0\,\text{or}\,y<1 \\ \frac{4{x}^{2}({y}^{2}-1)}{3{y}^{2}}, & 0\le x\le 1,\,1\le y\le 2 \\ {F}_{X}(x), & 0\le x\le 1,\,y>2 \\ {F}_{Y}(y), & x>1,\,1\le y\le 2 \\ 1, & x>1,\,y>2.\end{aligned}
$$

where ${F}_{X}$ and ${F}_{Y}$ are the marginal CDFs of $X$ and $Y,$ respectively. Find the joint PDF $f(x,y)$ for $0\le x\le 1$ and $1\le y\le 2.$
question.worked_solution:
Since the partial derivatives of $F(x,y)$ are defined, the joint probability density function $f(x,y)$ is determined by

$$
f(x,y)=\frac{{∂}^{2}}{∂x∂y}F(x,y).
$$

For $0\le x\le 1$ and $1\le y\le 2,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & =\frac{{∂}^{2}}{∂x∂y}F(x,y) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{4{x}^{2}({y}^{2}-1)}{3{y}^{2}})) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{4}{3}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(1-\frac{1}{{y}^{2}})) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{4}{3}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{2}{{y}^{3}}) \\  & =\frac{8}{3{y}^{3}}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{8}{3{y}^{3}}\cdot 2x \\  & =\frac{16x}{3{y}^{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Otherwise, $f(x,y)=0.$
Therefore, we have

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{16x}{3{y}^{3}}, & 0\le x\le 1,\,1\le y\le 2 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$
